verses.original: יֵ֣שׁ רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר רָאִ֖יתִי תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ הִ֖יא וְרַבָּ֥ה עַל־ הָאָדָֽם׃
verses.transliteration: yêš rā·‘āh ’ă·šer rā·’î·ṯî ta·ḥaṯ haš·šā·meš hî wə·rab·bāh ‘al- hā·’ā·ḏām
verses.literal: There is another evil - I have seen under the sun and it weighs heavily upon mankind

verses.original: הָאֱלֹהִ֡ים יִתֶּן־ ל֣וֹ אִ֣ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עֹשֶׁר֩ וּנְכָסִ֨ים וְכָב֜וֹד חָסֵ֥ר וְֽאֵינֶ֨נּוּ לְנַפְשׁ֣וֹ׀ מִכֹּ֣ל אֲשֶׁר־ יִתְאַוֶּ֗ה הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ וְלֹֽא־ יַשְׁלִיטֶ֤נּוּ לֶאֱכֹ֣ל מִמֶּ֔נּוּ כִּ֛י אִ֥ישׁ נָכְרִ֖י יֹֽאכֲלֶ֑נּוּ זֶ֥ה הֶ֛בֶל וָחֳלִ֥י רָ֖ע הֽוּא׃
verses.transliteration: hā·’ĕ·lō·hîm yit·ten- lōw ’îš ’ă·šer ‘ō·šer ū·nə·ḵā·sîm wə·ḵā·ḇō·wḏ ḥā·sêr wə·’ê·nen·nū lə·nap̄·šōw mik·kōl ’ă·šer- yiṯ·’aw·weh hā·’ĕ·lō·hîm wə·lō- yaš·lî·ṭen·nū le·’ĕ·ḵōl mim·men·nū kî ’îš nā·ḵə·rî yō·ḵă·len·nū zeh he·ḇel wā·ḥo·lî rā‘ hū
verses.literal: God gives a man - riches wealth and honor so that he lacks nothing his heart - - desires but God does not allow him to enjoy them - Instead a stranger . . . will enjoy them This is futile and a grievous affliction . . .

verses.original: אִם־ אִ֣ישׁ יוֹלִ֣יד מֵאָ֡ה יִֽחְיֶ֜ה רַבּ֨וֹת וְשָׁנִים֩ וְרַ֣ב׀ שֶׁיִּהְי֣וּ יְמֵֽי־ שָׁנָ֗יו וְנַפְשׁוֹ֙ לֹא־ תִשְׂבַּ֣ע מִן־ הַטּוֹבָ֔ה לֹא־ הָ֣יְתָה לּ֑וֹ וְגַם־ קְבוּרָ֖ה אָמַ֕רְתִּי הַנָּֽפֶל׃ ט֥וֹב מִמֶּ֖נּוּ
verses.transliteration: ’im- ’îš yō·w·lîḏ mê·’āh yiḥ·yeh rab·bō·wṯ wə·šā·nîm wə·raḇ še·yih·yū yə·mê- šā·nāw wə·nap̄·šōw lō- ṯiś·ba‘ min- haṭ·ṭō·w·ḇāh lō- hā·yə·ṯāh lōw wə·ḡam- qə·ḇū·rāh ’ā·mar·tî han·nā·p̄el ṭō·wḇ mim·men·nū
verses.literal: - A man may father a hundred [children] and live for many years yet no matter how long - he lives . . . if he vvv is unsatisfied with his prosperity and does not . . . even receive a proper burial I say that a stillborn child is better off than he

verses.original: כִּֽי־ בָּ֖א בַהֶ֥בֶל יֵלֵ֑ךְ וּבַחֹ֣שֶׁךְ שְׁמ֥וֹ יְכֻסֶּֽה׃ וּבַחֹ֖שֶׁךְ
verses.transliteration: kî- bā ḇa·he·ḇel yê·lêḵ ū·ḇa·ḥō·šeḵ šə·mōw yə·ḵus·seh ū·ḇa·ḥō·šeḵ
verses.literal: For [a stillborn child] enters in futility and departs in darkness and his name is shrouded in obscurity

verses.original: לָזֶ֖ה גַּם־ לֹא־ רָאָ֖ה שֶׁ֥מֶשׁ וְלֹ֣א יָדָ֑ע נַ֥חַת מִזֶּֽה׃
verses.transliteration: lā·zeh gam- lō- rā·’āh še·meš wə·lō yā·ḏā‘ na·ḥaṯ miz·zeh
verses.literal: [The child] though neither seeing the sun nor knowing anything has more rest than [that man]

verses.original: וְאִלּ֣וּ חָיָ֗ה אֶ֤לֶף שָׁנִים֙ פַּעֲמַ֔יִם לֹ֣א רָאָ֑ה וְטוֹבָ֖ה הֲלֹ֛א הַכֹּ֥ל הוֹלֵֽךְ׃ אֶל־ אֶחָ֖ד מָק֥וֹם
verses.transliteration: wə·’il·lū ḥā·yāh ’e·lep̄ šā·nîm pa·‘ă·ma·yim lō rā·’āh wə·ṭō·w·ḇāh hă·lō hak·kōl hō·w·lêḵ ’el- ’e·ḥāḏ mā·qō·wm
verses.literal: even if he lives a thousand years twice over but fails to enjoy his prosperity Do not all go to the same place

verses.original: כָּל־ הָאָדָ֖ם עֲמַ֥ל לְפִ֑יהוּ וְגַם־ הַנֶּ֖פֶשׁ לֹ֥א תִמָּלֵֽא׃
verses.transliteration: kāl- hā·’ā·ḏām ‘ă·mal lə·p̄î·hū wə·ḡam- han·ne·p̄eš lō ṯim·mā·lê
verses.literal: All a man’s labor [is] for his mouth yet his appetite is never satisfied

verses.original: מַה־ יּוֹתֵ֥ר כִּ֛י לֶחָכָ֖ם מִֽן־ הַכְּסִ֑יל מַה־ לֶּעָנִ֣י יוֹדֵ֔עַ לַהֲלֹ֖ךְ נֶ֥גֶד הַחַיִּֽים׃
verses.transliteration: mah- yō·w·ṯêr kî le·ḥā·ḵām min- hak·kə·sîl mah- le·‘ā·nî yō·w·ḏê·a‘ la·hă·lōḵ ne·ḡeḏ ha·ḥay·yîm
verses.literal: What advantage then has the wise man over the fool What [gain comes] to the poor man who knows how to conduct himself before others

verses.original: ט֛וֹב עֵינַ֖יִם מַרְאֵ֥ה מֵֽהֲלָךְ־ נָ֑פֶשׁ זֶ֥ה גַּם־ הֶ֖בֶל וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ׃
verses.transliteration: ṭō·wḇ ‘ê·na·yim mar·’êh mê·hă·lāḵ- nā·p̄eš zeh gam- he·ḇel ū·rə·‘ūṯ rū·aḥ
verses.literal: Better what the eye can see than the wandering of desire This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind

verses.original: מַה־ שֶּֽׁהָיָ֗ה נִקְרָ֣א שְׁמ֔וֹ כְּבָר֙ וְנוֹדָ֖ע אֲשֶׁר־ אָדָ֑ם ה֣וּא וְלֹא־ יוּכַ֣ל לָדִ֔ין עִ֥ם שֶׁהַתְקִיף מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃
verses.transliteration: mah- še·hā·yāh niq·rā šə·mōw kə·ḇār wə·nō·w·ḏā‘ ’ă·šer- ’ā·ḏām hū wə·lō- yū·ḵal lā·ḏîn ‘im šɛ·haṯ·qīp̄ mim·men·nū
verses.literal: Whatever exists was named . . . long ago and it is known what man [is] but he cannot . . . contend with one stronger than he

verses.original: כִּ֛י יֵשׁ־ הַרְבֵּ֖ה דְּבָרִ֥ים מַרְבִּ֣ים הָ֑בֶל מַה־ יֹּתֵ֖ר לָאָדָֽם׃
verses.transliteration: kî yêš- har·bêh də·ḇā·rîm mar·bîm hā·ḇel mah- yō·ṯêr lā·’ā·ḏām
verses.literal: For vvv the more words the more futility and how does that profit anyone

verses.original: כִּ֣י מִֽי־ יוֹדֵעַ֩ מַה־ טּ֨וֹב לָֽאָדָ֜ם בַּֽחַיִּ֗ים מִסְפַּ֛ר יְמֵי־ וְיַעֲשֵׂ֣ם הֶבְל֖וֹ חַיֵּ֥י כַּצֵּ֑ל אֲשֶׁר֙ מִֽי־ יַגִּ֣יד לָֽאָדָ֔ם מַה־ יִּהְיֶ֥ה אַחֲרָ֖יו תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃
verses.transliteration: kî mî- yō·w·ḏê·a‘ mah- ṭō·wḇ lā·’ā·ḏām ba·ḥay·yîm mis·par yə·mê- wə·ya·‘ă·śêm heḇ·lōw ḥay·yê kaṣ·ṣêl ’ă·šer mî- yag·gîḏ lā·’ā·ḏām mah- yih·yeh ’a·ḥă·rāw ta·ḥaṯ haš·šā·meš
verses.literal: For who knows what is good for a man - during the few days [in which] he passes through his fleeting life like a shadow - Who can tell a man what will come after him under the sun
